reviewer: Codex main reviewer; read the complete retained six-paragraph NIST narrative, article title and visible publication dateline. A separate read-only reviewer checked source-native identity candidates.
prior_exposure: Outcome-exposed follow-up from the full 45-group NIST PMT screen. The reviewer has already read the later narrative and frozen original-project diagnostic. This is retrospective source-claim acceptance, not independent outcome labeling, representative historical coverage or blind detector/forecast evaluation.
interpretation: Accept three atomic attributes of the existing Coherent Sherman facility described by NIST: indium-phosphide material, 150 mm wafer size and high-volume production scale. All three share one source narrative and are not three independent observations. The narrative separately says proposed funding will support expansion, and future equipment and cleanroom capacity will be added. The up-to-$50-million letter of intent is not a finalized award, replacement of the original PMT, expansion completion or measured output. Retain the 150mm (6-inch) literal in local evidence; use exact stated 150 mm rather than converting six inches. June 16 is the publication day, not HVM onset or a physical-effective date. Source statements remain null-effective, null-confidence and excluded from physical-current claims.
identity_review: Create a new source-native facility, without canonical assignment. Existing Sherman sites dbb2f6db-1c37-5482-a718-954595fceebe and 7bdc424d-10a3-58a7-9447-82633eab5fc4 belong to GlobalWafers and Texas Instruments project contexts. EPA site 40512b6a-4d7d-585e-86f5-4e9f93d0db5e (epa:frs:110064117290, FINISAR SHERMAN) is a possible research lead only: this NIST narrative supplies no street address, registry identifier, Finisar identity or ownership bridge. City-name matching is insufficient. No old identity, relationship, project group or outcome is altered.
